panels.description: Wide, full page width. The mandapa of Padmanabhaswamy at night. Oil lamps in brass holders burn along every wall and pillar, their flames doubled in the polished stone floor until the whole hall seems to float on fire. Carved granite pillars recede into shadow. Beyond an open outer doorway, monsoon rain falls in a silver sheet. The nobles of Travancore stand packed in ranks, bare-chested in temple fashion, fine mundus and shoulder cloths, gold at their ears and throats catching the lamplight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The monsoon of 1750, three days after Kottarakkara fell. The king called every noble in the kingdom to Padmanabhaswamy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not for war council. Not for treaty.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some had lost kinsmen. Some had lost lands. All had learned to bow.

panels.description: The front ranks from behind and a little above. Nobles in order of importance, composed faces in profile, jewels glinting. In the front rank, one clear gap on the stone where no one stands, a single lamp's reflection lying in it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Near the front was the place where Padmini would once have stood, stick planted, eyes sharp.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Fever had taken her months before. The gap she left was as visible as any banner.

panels.description: Nagoji at the back of the hall among the lesser officers. He is Ananthan Pillai in temple dress: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, NO turban, cream mundu, shoulder cloth over a bare chest, silver chain of office, no forehead marks, no sacred thread; strong cheekbones, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. No coat inside the temple. Two nobles in the rank ahead glance back at him sidelong.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi had not come.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her absence was noted, weighed, filed away.

panels.description: The temple attendant (young and slight, bare-chested, plain short mundu, hair in a small knot at the crown) lowers a great conch from his lips. A herald (middle-aged, bare-chested, white mundu, a plain staff of office) steps into the lamplight before the assembly, chin raised, voice trained to cut through drums and crowd. The herald and the attendant are NOT priests: do not use the temple-priest reference for either.

copy.speaker: HERALD
copy.text: Listen and witness.

copy.speaker: HERALD
copy.text: His Highness Sree Anizham Thirunal Marthanda Varma, Maharaja of Travancore.

copy.speaker: HERALD
copy.text: Victor of Colachel. Breaker of the Eight Houses.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. At the far doorway, Marthanda Varma enters. V13 varma-v1 face, aged: grey hair in a low knot, plain white mundu, bare torso with the sacred thread across his chest, no crown, no jewels, no headwear. He carries a sword flat across both palms, its hilt wrapped in silk, its blade catching the flames. Every head in the hall has turned.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had heard him called Varma, called Maharaja, called tiger.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Hearing the whole weight of him spoken aloud inside a temple made the air feel thinner.

panels.description: Low wide shot down the aisle of lamps. Varma (aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, plain white mundu, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, no jewels) walks the length of the mandapa alone, small between the silent ranks, the sword across his palms. At the far end, before the sanctum, a row of temple priests chanting. The chief priest uses the V13 temple-priest face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The priests' chant was a river of sound. It had flowed here long before any of us were born.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It would flow long after we were dust.

panels.description: The threshold of the sanctum. Varma from behind, dwarfed, grey low knot and bare back. Through the doors, Lord Padmanabha reclining on the great serpent Anantha, seen only in fragments of gold and shadow: a vast shoulder, a resting hand, the many hoods of the serpent rising above. Draw it with reverence. The hoods seem to lean in the flicker of the lamps.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A thousand eyes, watching the one man who dared to stand before them.

panels.description: Full-width dark strip, about a third of the page tall, between 2.2 and 2.4. Beneath the flagged floor, a vault in blackness. Heaped coins and old chests catch a single thread of light in the centre of the strip: Roman gold, Venetian ducats, Dutch guilders, coins of empires long gone. Keep the left and right ends of the strip in deep black for the two captions, so the lettering never sits on the coins.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The true weight of this place was not in the stone. It was under it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The black gold of pepper, turned into the yellow gold of offerings. Enough to buy the Dutch East India Company three times over.

panels.description: Varma kneeling on the cold stone before the threshold, head bowed: grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, plain white mundu. Behind him the nobles are out of focus and utterly still. A lamp in the near foreground, its flame bending.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The silence was absolute. I could hear the hiss of oil in the nearest lamp.

panels.description: Tight, full-width strip. His hands lowering the sword to the stone, point toward the god, the silk-wrapped hilt touching down last.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It did not clatter. He laid it down the way a father lays down a sleeping child.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One soft, final click.

panels.description: Varma still kneeling, face raised toward the sanctum, lit gold from within: aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, no jewels.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: From this day, I am no longer king of this land.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I am only the servant of He who lies here.

panels.description: Wide, from the back of the hall over the heads of the nobles. The kneeling figure is small and bright at the far end. His balloons reach all the way back to us.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: All that I have taken, all that I have built, all that I have paid for in blood and exile and broken houses...

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I give to Him. The kingdom is His. I merely hold it in trust.

panels.description: The priests raise their hands, the chant swelling. In the foreground, an old noble's face, eyes wet, lips moving in prayer.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The pious among them saw a king humbling himself before his god.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Others saw the trap.

panels.description: At the back of the hall, three men side by side facing the sanctum. Left foreground: Nagoji (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, bare chest, cream mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain of office clearly visible, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin), eyes forward on the sanctum. Centre: the whispering chief, a minor chief from the northern marches (heavy-set, older, shaven head with a small front tuft, heavy gold ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth, grey stubble, no thick moustache), leaning right toward his neighbour, eyes wide, voice kept under the chant. Right: the neighbour (younger and thin, hair loose, plain shoulder cloth).

copy.speaker: CHIEF (whisper)
copy.text: He has given the land to god, so that he can keep it forever.

panels.description: The same three, closer on the chief and his neighbour. The neighbour (younger, thin, hair loose) lips twitching, not smiling. The chief (heavy-set, shaven head with a front tuft, gold ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth) goes on, still leaning in. Nagoji's shoulder and silver chain at the left edge of frame.

copy.speaker: CHIEF (whisper)
copy.text: Who can take from a god what a god owns? Not Mysore. Not the Nizam. Not the Dutch.

copy.speaker: CHIEF (whisper)
copy.text: Not even a woman with a legitimate claim.

panels.description: Ramayyan Dalawa near the front, side-on to the sanctum: thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle under one arm. He is not watching the king and not watching the god. His eyes move along the bowed rows, lingering on a stiff shoulder here, a lifted chin there.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He was checking the mortar on this new wall they had built.

panels.description: Nagoji, close, lamplight across half his face (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, bare shoulders, shoulder cloth, silver chain, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, no forehead marks), looking from Ramayyan to the kneeling king.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I understood then.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had built walls of stone and armies of men. Now he built a wall of faith, and it was the strongest of them all.

panels.description: Varma rising from his knees (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, plain white mundu). The sword stays where he laid it at the threshold, drinking the lamplight. From the side, the temple attendant (young and slight, bare-chested, plain short mundu, hair in a small knot) steps forward carrying a bundle of thin coconut-leaf ribs. The nobles shift and turn to one another, lips moving behind raised hands.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But he was not finished.

panels.description: Inset, tight. A Kerala broom: a bundle of thin coconut-leaf ribs bound with coir at one end, no wooden pole, its tips worn ragged from honest work. It passes from the attendant's hands into the king's.

Full width, bottom. Varma bent low, one knee on the stone, sweeping before the sanctum with short, deliberate strokes of the handleless broom, gathering dust, scattered flower petals, ash from a thousand offerings: grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, plain white mundu. The nobles in the background frozen, their hands dropped, their mouths closed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The murmuring died. I could hear the bristles scraping on the stone.

panels.description: Large, top half of the page. High angle down the long pillared corridor that runs around the temple, lamps receding in two long lines. Far down it, one small bare-chested figure bent low over a short handleless broom of coconut-leaf ribs, mid-stroke. Nobles stand at the edges like statues. Past the outer wall, rain on the dark leaves of the serpent grove.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The king who had broken the Dutch, who had shattered the Eight Houses, who had built an army that made Mysore think twice.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Like any temple servant.

panels.description: Varma in the near foreground, down on his knees on the stone, sweeping with the short coconut-rib broom, his face lowered to the work (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest). Behind him, standing among the nobles and watching him: the whispering chief from page 3 (heavy-set, shaven head with a small front tuft, heavy gold ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth, grey stubble). The knowing look has gone out of the chief's face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was not theatre. This was a man who meant what he said.

panels.description: Back before the sanctum. Varma standing (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest), his mundu grey with dust, his hands grey with ash. He hands the broom back to the temple attendant (young and slight, bare-chested, plain short mundu, hair in a small knot).

Nagoji's point of view across the hall. Varma has turned to face the assembly (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, dust on his mundu), and his eyes have found Nagoji's.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: There was no triumph in his gaze. Only the weariness of a man who had finally placed his last piece on the board and could only wait to see if the game was won.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Row after row of nobles' heads going down across the mandapa. In the nearest bowing row, the whispering chief, his red-bordered shoulder cloth and shaven head readable. Beyond the bowing rows, Varma standing at the sanctum threshold and facing them (bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, grey low knot), the one head not bowed. The sword lies gleaming on the stone just behind his feet, at the god's threshold. The priests intone.

copy.speaker: PRIESTS
copy.text: Padmanabha Dasa.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Servant of Padmanabha.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The land belonged to god now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: And god's servant still held the sword.

panels.description: Wide. A fort courtyard in early evening. Above the gate, the Travancore banner, a silver conch on red, lifting in the wind. Revathi Bayi stands alone on the flagstones looking up at it: deep indigo sari with gold, grey threading her black hair, jasmine in her braid, the tali on its yellow thread, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline. Behind her, in a doorway, Nagoji in uniform: white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, silver chain, sword at his hip; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One week later.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That banner flew now over all the lands that had once been a dozen kingdoms.

panels.description: Two-shot. Revathi (indigo sari, jasmine braid, grey threading) still faces the banner, not him. Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban) has come a few steps into the courtyard.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: She reached Kochi. They gave her a small house. She tends a garden now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am glad she lives.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Are you?

panels.description: Nagoji, silent, jaw set, the banner's shadow across him (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Her next balloon comes in from off-panel and lands on his face.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: You could have let her go. During the battle. You were close enough.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: She was trying to reach the boats.

panels.description: Revathi turns her head to him at last. No heat in her face, only weariness.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did not see her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Liar.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Perhaps.

panels.description: Close on Revathi, looking at him as if seeing him for the first time. Nagoji soft in the background (white coat, topknot, NO turban).

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You have made your choice. Completely now. There is no more standing with one foot in each river.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are his man. His sword. His builder.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Yes.

panels.description: Wide two-shot, a long stretch of flagstone between them. Revathi (indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, grey threading, tali) and Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban).

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And I am still hers. Her kinswoman. Her blood. The one who stood beside you in the same hall while you burned her claim.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Velinadu sent no men against us. You kept your doors closed.

panels.description: Revathi turning away a step, toward the gate, her face in profile against the evening light.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Closed is not the same as open.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Silence is not the same as support.

panels.description: She turns back.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We will not be enemies. Velinadu and Travancore need each other too much for that.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: But we will never be simple. You chose. So did I.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What did you choose?

panels.description: Tight on Revathi.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: To remember.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: When everyone else forgets what this cost, I will remember. Savitri's face. Her garden in Kochi. The laugh she will never laugh again.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi walking out through the gate into the low gold evening, small, not looking back. Nagoji in the near foreground, still (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban), the banner above them both. Her last balloons trail back to him; his caption sits low beside him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Someone has to carry that weight. It will not be you. It will not be him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: So it will be me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Another world, where kings did not have to break houses to build kingdoms.

panels.description: Wide. Mavelikkara, 1753. A pavilion table. A Dutch East India Company commissioner in 1750s dress (knee-length skirted dark coat with wide turned-back cuffs, long waistcoat, knee breeches, white lace-edged stock, powdered bag-wig, his tricorn on the table) signs with a quill. Company soldiers in blue coats stand at the back. Across the table, Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) watches the pen, palm-leaf bundle at his elbow. No lettering on the document or on any flag.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Great Offering did what accounts and cannons could not.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three years later the Dutch came back to Mavelikkara. This time they did not just bow.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had sold their allies to save their trade.

panels.description: Night. A fort rampart, the stone still wet. Varma alone at the parapet, staring out at nothing: aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, plain white mundu, a plain shoulder cloth over one shoulder, the sacred thread across his chest, no jewels, no headwear. Nagoji in uniform (white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud) coming along the wall walk toward him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But the final cost of that peace was not written in ink.

panels.description: Varma, not turning, speaking to the dark.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Nizam sent an envoy last month. Mysore's man was here before that.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The British build at Madras as if they mean to stay forever. And the Dutch, even now, count their losses and plan their next move.

panels.description: Varma turns to face Nagoji (aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, plain shoulder cloth, sacred thread across his chest, no jewels).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This is what I was always building toward. Not conquering for glory. Consolidating for survival.

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder onto Nagoji, close, his face unreadable (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Varma's grey low knot and shoulder soft at the near edge of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Every house I absorbed, every chief I bent, every woman I exiled, it was all for this:

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: a kingdom strong enough that when they come, any of them, all of them, they will find more than pepper and prayers.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the cost?

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder (grey low knot, sacred thread, shoulder cloth) toward the dark: far off, the small lamps of distant forts on the hills. He is looking back out over the dark as he speaks.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The cost is that men like Savitri's kinsman die in rooms they cannot leave.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That women like her tend gardens in foreign cities and curse my name.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That Revathi looks at me like I am the disease I claimed to cure.

panels.description: Tight on his hands gripping the parapet, knuckles pale against the wet stone.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do you think I do not feel it? Do you think I do not wake in the night and hear them?

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Every name. Every claim I denied. Every law I bent or broke.

panels.description: Varma's face, close, his voice cracking. Behind him, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: the same memory as the Chapter 27 stain (7.4), a sunlit courtyard long ago and young Savitri of Kottarakkara, a girl in her teens, her head thrown back in laughter. Her face is Savitri's Chapter 27 face made young. She wears a cream cloth with a red-and-gold border and simple gold at her ears and throat. NOT Revathi: no indigo, no jasmine braid, no tali, no flat-coin necklace.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I remember her laugh. From when we were young.

panels.description: Varma in profile against the night sky (grey low knot, sacred thread across his chest), his grip on the parapet loosening, one hand lying open on the wet stone. Nagoji small and out of focus behind him (white coat, topknot).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And I remember the moment, in that tent, when I looked in her eyes and saw that she would never laugh again.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I did that. For this.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Wide over the rampart: the king's arm opening out toward the dark kingdom below, the lamps of forts on the far hills, the pale line of a road, the ordered cookfires of an army camp. Two small figures on the wall: Varma bare-chested in white, Nagoji in the white coat.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: For this.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had no comfort to offer.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some wounds are the price of building. Some prices are too high to name, but too necessary not to pay.

panels.description: Wide. Evening, a quiet corner of Udayagiri Fort. A small chapel of local stone with a simple wooden cross above its door. Through the open door: De Lannoy (tall, pale grey hair, clean-shaven, a worn white Travancore coat over a plain buff waistcoat, no red waistcoat) kneeling in the front pew with his head bowed; Father Duarte at a small altar, hands raised (thin, white-haired, scholar's stoop, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO white Roman collar tab, no stole or chasuble). Nagoji in uniform (white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin) waits outside by the doorpost.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Udayagiri Fort. The Dutch had sailed away with their diminished pride.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Latin words that meant nothing to me, and everything to De Lannoy.

panels.description: De Lannoy (tall, pale grey hair, worn white coat, buff waistcoat) stepping out into the evening light, a peace in his face rarely seen in the war halls. Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban) at the doorpost, facing him.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Pillai. You do not usually visit this part of the fort.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I do not usually find two Europeans praying to their god in a kingdom that just surrendered itself to ours.

panels.description: Duarte in the doorway behind De Lannoy: the scholar's stoop, the ink-stained fingers, white hair, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO white Roman collar tab.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Father Duarte. I remembered those eyes from the dungeon. Now they held less guilt than acceptance.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: The Maharaja permits us this small space. We ask nothing of him but the right to serve.

panels.description: De Lannoy (worn white coat, buff waistcoat, pale grey hair) lays his palm flat on the chapel's stone doorframe as he speaks, the walls of the fort he designed rising behind him.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: And to pray. A man needs something beyond walls and accounts.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Otherwise the walls become a prison and the accounts become chains.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The three of them at the foot of the fort wall in the low evening light, the chapel door behind them. Left to right: De Lannoy (worn white coat, buff waistcoat, tall, pale grey hair, clean-shaven), Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache), Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab). As De Lannoy answers, Duarte steps forward out of the group toward Nagoji, his callused, ink-stained right hand just starting to lift.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: A Maratha cavalryman, a Dutch artillerist, a Portuguese priest.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Twenty years ago our peoples were killing each other across three continents. Now we stand under the same banner.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: The banner does not ask where we came from. Only where we stand now.

panels.description: Duarte's right hand, callused and ink-stained, stopped in the air between him and Nagoji, the black cassock sleeve fallen back from the wrist. Hold it. Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban) watching the hand. Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab).
The hand completes the motion: a sign of the cross in Nagoji's direction, quick but deliberate. Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab).

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: I do not do this to convert you. It is the only blessing I know how to give.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: And you have earned a blessing, Ananthan Pillai. Whatever you believe.

panels.description: A lighter beat. De Lannoy (worn white coat, buff waistcoat) half-smiling; Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, NO white Roman collar tab) with the ghost of a smile.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Even Ramayyan visited once. He spent the whole time examining the stonework rather than the altar.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: He said the mortar was acceptable. High praise, from him.

panels.description: De Lannoy (tall, pale grey hair, worn white coat) looking back through the open chapel door at the floor before the altar. Quiet.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: When I die, I have asked to be buried here. In this fort I helped design. Under a stone that says I served Travancore.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. De Lannoy at left, his right hand gripping Nagoji's forearm; Nagoji at centre (white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin); Duarte at right beside them (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab). The fort wall behind, the evening sky above it.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: We are all servants now. You serve Padmanabha through the king. I serve Padmanabha through the walls.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: It is a strange household. But it holds.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The kingdom had absorbed us all. And somehow, in the absorbing, it had made us more than we had been alone.

panels.description: Wide. A star-fort rampart at dusk, monsoon clouds building over the sea. Nagoji old now, on the nagoji-v2 later-life sheet: grey-streaked hair in a topknot, white mundu with a gold border, its end draped over one shoulder, no coat, NO turban, the same thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, leaning on the parapet. Beside him a young Travancore officer: about twenty, round-faced, slighter than Nagoji, clean-shaven with no moustache, no ear stud, hair in a small Nair tuft at the crown, in a white European-cut coat and red waistcoat. The officer is NOT Nagoji: do not use the Nagoji reference for him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Years later, when my joints ached with old battles.

copy.speaker: OFFICER
copy.text: What was Travancore like, before it was Travancore?

panels.description: Inset. Remembered: the map on the war-hall table, a painted map of the south of the peninsula with the sea to the left. Colour regions: red inland to the north (Mysore), black far to the north (the Nizam), brown to the east (Arcot), small blue marks at the coastal forts (the Europeans), and many small pale patches crowded along the south-west coast. No place names, labels or lettering anywhere on the map.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Red for Mysore. Black for the Nizam. Brown for Arcot. Blue for the Europeans.

panels.description: Nagoji (later-life: grey-streaked topknot, white gold-bordered mundu over one shoulder, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin), turned toward the young officer (round face, no moustache, small Nair tuft, white coat).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It was smaller. And more divided. And more free, in some ways.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And more vulnerable.

copy.speaker: OFFICER
copy.text: Do you miss it?

panels.description: Large panel. What the wall looks down on, in three layers. Foreground, the yard below: Nair musketeers drilling by volley in white Travancore coats over white mundus, cross-belts, long muskets, a red standard with a silver conch above them; NOT red coats, NOT blue coats, no tricorns. Middle distance: a shore battery, its guns trained on the sea. Beyond: horsemen riding through the surf without flinching, and past them Marakkar coastal craft (Malabar pattamars with lateen sails, not European galleons) with the red silver-conch flag at the masthead. No lettering on any flag.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When I first washed ashore, the king borrowed lancers from Madurai and begged muskets from English factors. His horses feared the sand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now there were fifty thousand men under arms. All of it paid for in pepper and blood.

panels.description: Nagoji close in the foreground (later-life: grey-streaked topknot, white gold-bordered mundu over one shoulder, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin), old eyes on the young man. The officer at the edge of frame (round face, no moustache, small tuft, white coat), polite and blank.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I miss what it cost.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had been born into the kingdom we built. He did not know what had been burned to make it.

panels.description: Faded, bleeding in from the panel edge like old ink: the Goa interrogation room from Chapter 1, framed low so the ceiling is out of frame. No nooses: if a rope shows at all, it hangs from an iron ring for binding wrists. Young Nagoji on the captivity sheet: torn ochre sleeveless tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged hands and wrists, ankle irons, barefoot, black hair loose with no grey, no topknot, no turban, light stubble at most; seated on the stool, wrists bound to its legs. The younger Duarte standing before him: dark-haired, thin, scholar's stoop, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO white Roman collar tab.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (faded)
copy.text: He seems to favour whoever has the better powder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That young man had been wrong. Belief had turned out to matter more than anything.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Just not the kind the priest was selling.

panels.description: Memory, lamplit. Revathi's western verandah on a wet night, years back, in their married years. Revathi: deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, grey threading in her black hair, the tali, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets; turning away toward a small girl, a niece and not Nagoji's child, running on the wet stone, one hand raised to scold. Nagoji behind her: Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, cream mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain, no knife at the waist, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin; mouth closed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One night on her western verandah, long before Savitri's banners rose, I almost told her I would lay down my marches if she asked.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words sat on my tongue like a loaded musket.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Perhaps that mercy was hers, not mine.

panels.description: Wide, split down the middle, the same rain falling across both halves. Left: a small garden in Kochi, Savitri elderly, in white, lines of care, among her plants; no jasmine, no indigo. Right: a Velinadu courtyard, Revathi elderly on the verandah: grey hair still braided with jasmine, deep indigo sari with gold, tali, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets; children running laughing through the wet corridors. Keep the left and right order: Kochi left, Velinadu right.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The monsoon came that year, as it always did.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (tag, left half)
copy.text: Kochi.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (tag, right half)
copy.text: Velinadu.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (right half)
copy.text: She remembered. The children in the rain carried my blood and hers.

panels.description: Large, bottom half of the page. Nagoji alone on the fort wall in the rain, face lifted to it, eyes closed: later-life sheet, grey-streaked hair in a topknot, white mundu with a gold border, its end draped over one shoulder, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, no coat, NO turban. Beyond and below him the whole kingdom under the same rain: forts, roads, fields, the grey sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here I stood guard over what we had built from the ashes of what they had lost.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That was the price. That was always the price.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some things do not wash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some things we carry.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: For as long as we live, and in the stories that outlast us.

frames.review_note: Clean. Standing ranks of bare-chested nobles in mundus and shoulder cloths, brass open-wick lamps doubled in the polished floor, carved pillars, open outer doorway with a silver sheet of rain, sanctum shown only as gold fragments. No painted text. Captions fit in the dark ceiling and pillar-capital band across the top and on the low-detail floor at lower right.

Minor issues only. The front-rank gap is fairly wide and could read as an aisle, but it is the only break in the rank and the single lamp reflection sits in it, so the beat comes through. The top band is busy with pillars, the rain doorway and the gold sanctum doors. Captions should go top-left over the doorway and pillars, or over the empty polished floor between the front rank and the sanctum steps (about y 0.26 to 0.33). Neither spot covers a face. No text, no complete deity and no anachronisms. The staff-holder's hand is sound. Everyone is standing, barefoot and bare-chested, which matches the 1.1 setting.

Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch28 temple row: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, silver chain with a medallion, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth on a bare chest, no forehead marks and no sacred thread. Two nobles in front of him glance at him sidelong, so the beat works. Weaker points: this assembly is SEATED, while 1.1 and the chosen 1.2 show standing ranks. Nagoji also faces the camera while the men behind him face away toward the sanctum. That reads as a portrait staging, not as him standing behind the rank. The young noble at right wears loose long curly hair, not a topknot. He has no moustache, so he does not read as a Nagoji double. Captions go in the upper corners over the pillar carvings at top-left and the sanctum and lamps at top-right, clear of all three faces. No text, no blood and hands are sound. Acceptable given it is the only candidate. Regenerate later only if the author wants the hall standing throughout.

Acceptable with minor deviations. The attendant still has the conch at his lips rather than lowering it; the beat (conch sounded, herald announcing) still reads. Both are correctly not priests: a young slight attendant in a short mundu with a crown knot, and a middle-aged herald in a white mundu with a staff, chin raised, mouth open. The nobles in front are seated, while 1.1 and 1.2 show them standing. A small seated statue in a side doorway at right reads as a carving, not the god. No painted text. The three herald balloons fit in the rain doorway at upper left and the dark ceiling band above the herald, clear of faces.

Acceptable. Varma matches the aged dedication sheet: grey hair drawn back into a low knot, moustache, bare torso with the sacred thread, plain white mundu, no jewels or headwear. He enters from the rain-filled far doorway, the silk-wrapped hilt and flame-lit blade held across his body, and every noble's head is turned toward him. Minor issues: he grips the hilt in his right hand with the blade resting on his left palm, rather than lying flat across both palms; the mundu has a thin gold hem border; the nobles are seated, while 1.1 has them standing. No painted text. The two captions fit in the dark carved pillar areas at the top, to the left and right of the doorway, clear of faces.

Clean. Varma seen from behind (grey low knot, bare back, sacred thread, white mundu with a thin gold hem border, no jewels) walks alone up the lamp-lined aisle between seated ranks of nobles, sword held level across his hands; chief priest at the far end matches the V13 temple-priest face, the other chanting priests are bearded and distinct. Rain only through the open outer doorway, as the setting specifies. Two grey-haired nobles in the ranks are older men, not Varma doubles. The dark ceiling between the pillars (top centre, roughly x 0.38 to 0.75, y 0.0 to 0.22) takes both captions clear of faces.

Clean. Varma from behind at the sanctum threshold (grey low knot, bare back, sacred thread, plain white mundu with a thin gold hem, no jewels), sword held level; through the gold doors only fragments of Padmanabha (a resting hand and forearm on the serpent coils) under five rising hoods, drawn reverently, never the whole god. He is less dwarfed than the script suggests, but the tall doors carry the scale. Same mandapa, lamps and rain-filled outer doorway as panel 1. Dark ceiling at upper left (x 0.05 to 0.3, y 0.0 to 0.2) holds the caption.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Acceptable with minor notes. Varma matches the aged dedication look (grey hair gathered in a knot at the back, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, sacred thread, bare torso, white mundu, no jewels), kneeling with head bowed, the sword across both open palms pointing toward the sanctum, which leads cleanly into 2.5; hands are sound. A foreground brass lamp with a bending flame sits at lower right as scripted. Minor: the nobles behind him are sharp, not out of focus, and they stand, while panel 1 showed seated ranks; the lead noble (dark-grey hair, curled moustache, gold necklaces and armbands) slightly echoes Varma's younger court look but is clearly a different man. Dark ceiling at top centre (x 0.3 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.15) holds the caption.

The framing is a medium shot of the whole kneeling figure, wider than the scripted tight strip on the hands. His moustache reads thinner and greyer than in 2.4. Accepted because the beat is clear: his hands lower a bare steel blade, point toward the sanctum, with a red silk-wrapped hilt that matches 1.5. The grey low knot, sacred thread, plain mundu and setting all match. Captions can sit over the shadowed pillars along the top or on the floor at lower left without touching his face, his hands or the sword.

Minor: a tiny gold speck just under the nose tip, at the top of the moustache (about 5 px at full size). It reads as a highlight at print size, but paint it out if it shows as a nose ornament. The mundu has gold kasavu borders rather than plain white, which matches the page 2 frames. Otherwise this is the aged varma-v1 face: grey hair in a low knot at the nape, sacred thread, bare torso, kneeling and lit gold from the sanctum, with rain in the outer doorway. There is no painted text, and the dark ceiling at top left and centre gives room for both balloons.

Clean. The wide shot is taken over the seated nobles' heads. Varma kneels small and bright at the far end, seen from behind, with a grey low knot, the sacred thread and a white mundu. The dark ceiling band above the sanctum and the upper pillars leaves room for the two balloons to run back toward the viewer.

Clean. Only the central chief priest carries the temple-priest sheet face; the other chanting priests have moustaches or beards and read as different men. In the foreground, the old noble has wet eyes and parted lips, with his hands joined in prayer, and the hands are sound. Both captions fit at the top corners, over the rain doorway on the left and the lamp tops on the right, clear of the raised hands.

Minor: Nagoji's jaw has light stubble shading, but there is no beard, and the curled moustache, small flush gold stud, topknot and grey temple are all correct. The silver chain of office shows clearly across his back. The chief's tuft sits at the crown rather than the front. The chief is heavy-set and shaven, with heavy gold ear-rings, a red-bordered shoulder cloth and grey stubble, and he leans right with a cupped hand toward the young, loose-haired neighbour. The balloon can sit in the upper band of pillars between Nagoji and the chief.

Minor: the clear space for the two balloons is the upper band above the heads (y below about 0.18), which is dark pillar and rain-doorway background and slightly tight; the chief's front tuft sits toward the crown rather than strictly at the front. Nagoji appears only as a shoulder and chest with the silver chain and medallion at the left edge, as the script asks. The chief matches panel 3.4: hoop earrings, red-bordered cloth, grey stubble, hand cupped at his mouth. Same mandapa, lamps and rain-lit outer doorway as 3.4. No painted text, balloons or anachronisms.

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, hands sound. He stands among the bowed rows with the sanctum behind him at right, and his eyes are on the rows. A noble at right lifts his chin, which fits the script's 'a lifted chin there'. The open outer doorway shows rain, as the setting requires. The caption fits the dark pillar and ceiling area in the upper middle. Minor: the nobles here are bowed low on the floor, while in 4.3 they sit and in 4.5 they stand.

Acceptable. Nagoji shows the Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a small flush gold ear stud, a silver chain, a bare chest with shoulder cloth and no forehead marks. His chin reads clean-shaven: there is only the faint ink hatching of the house style, no beard. He looks aside toward the sanctum side. Minor: the lamplight is more even across his face than the 'half his face' the script asks for, and the shoulder cloth has a gold stripe. Both captions fit in the dark carved ceiling area at the upper right (about x 0.6 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.22) without touching his face.

Acceptable, with minor issues. Varma, aged varma-v1, is rising from one knee with a hand on his knee: grey low knot, moustache, sacred thread, no jewels. The young attendant has a small knot and steps in holding a bundle of thin ribs. Nobles on both sides whisper behind raised hands. Minor: (1) Varma's and the attendant's mundus have a thin gold border rather than plain white, though the neighbouring ch28 frames draw Varma the same way. (2) The sword on the stone is drawn as an ornate gold sheathed sword, not the bare blade with a red silk hilt from 2.5, and it lies behind him to the left rather than clearly at the sanctum threshold. (3) The broom ribs are pale straw here and darker brown in 4.4 and 4.5. The caption fits the upper middle among the dark pillar tops.

v03 (the newest version) is acceptable. It is a tight handover of a handleless coconut-rib broom bound with coir, with ragged tips, passing from the attendant to Varma in the same lamplit mandapa as 4.3 and 4.5: granite pillars, brass open-wick lamps, rain through the outer doorway on the right. Varma is cropped just below the mouth. Only his chin, neck and a grey low knot at the back show, with bare torso, sacred thread and plain white mundu, and no jewels. All four hands are sound. There is no text, no blood and nothing anachronistic. The panel has no lettering. Minor faults: (1) The inking is flatter and cleaner than the more painterly 4.3 and 4.5. (2) The visible chin has light grey stubble, which hardly shows at inset size. (3) The attendant's mundu is plain white, while in 4.3 it has a thin gold edge. The other versions are worse. v01 shows Varma's whole face with no moustache, which breaks his sheet, and it is wider than the script's 'inset, tight'. v02 is photorealistic, which breaks the style rule.

Acceptable. Aged Varma kneels low before the golden sanctum doors, sweeping scattered flower petals with a short handleless rib broom: moustache, grey low knot, sacred thread, white mundu, hands sound. In the background the nobles stand frozen with their hands dropped and clasped and their mouths closed. Rain shows through the outer doorway. The frame is the required 3:1 strip, and the faces sit in the middle band. Minor: he is down on both knees rather than one, and his mundu has the thin gold border used throughout the chapter. The caption fits the dark ceiling and pillar tops in the upper middle (about x 0.42 to 0.6, y 0.02 to 0.18).

Minor only: Varma is in the middle distance, not the very small far figure the script asks for, and the high angle is moderate. Grey low knot, sacred thread, moustache, no jewels, short coconut-rib broom held mid-stroke, nobles at the edges, rain on the grove past the outer wall. The upper frame is busy with pillars, so both captions belong on the clear lamplit floor in the lower centre (x 0.25-0.80, y 0.65-0.95), which has no faces.

Minor: the chief has a short grey beard rather than stubble, and his look is a troubled hand-to-chin frown, which still reads as the knowing look gone. Varma kneels with the short broom, has a grey low knot and sacred thread, and wears no jewels. The sanctum shows only gold fragments, with no whole idol. The caption can sit in the dark low-detail area at top centre (x 0.48-0.73, y 0.0-0.13).

Minor: the broom here is a longer bundle than the short broom in panels 1-2, though it is still handleless coconut ribs. A soft gold idol-like shape shows through the sanctum door, but it is blurred, partial and half hidden by the attendant, so it reads as fragments of gold. Varma's mundu is dusty and his hands are ash-grey. He has a grey low knot at the nape and the sacred thread. The attendant is young and slight, with a short mundu and a small top knot. No lettering is needed.

None significant. Varma has turned to the assembly and looks toward the viewer from Nagoji's point of view. He has a grey low knot, the sacred thread and a dust-marked mundu, and wears no jewels. Nagoji is not drawn. The long caption fits in the dark empty ceiling at top right (x 0.55-0.88, y 0.0-0.18).

Minor: several chanting priests stand upright beside Varma, which softens 'the one head not bowed', though he is still the central, framed figure. The sword lies beside rather than directly behind his feet. The bowing chief shows his shaven head and red-bordered cloth but no visible gold ear-rings. Only the lamp-bearing chief priest has the temple-priest face, so there are no doubles. Lettering space is tight. Put the PRIESTS balloon over the rain at top left (x 0.04-0.14, y 0.0-0.15), with its tail to the lamp-bearing chief priest. Put the captions over the anonymous bowed backs in the bottom-left and bottom-right corners (y 0.85-1.0), clear of the chief, Varma and the sword.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet and bible row (indigo and gold sari, grey streak, jasmine braid, coin necklace, tali on yellow thread, armlets, sandalwood line). Nagoji in the doorway matches (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, sword, grey topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Banner is plain red with a silver conch and no lettering. Open sky at upper centre takes both captions.

Minor: Revathi is seen from behind with her head in slight profile to frame right, so whether she faces the banner or him is a little ambiguous. Nagoji's hair hangs looser than in 6.1 and his sword is not visible. His face matches: clean chin, curled moustache, grey temples, small gold stud. Open sky upper middle and right, plus open flagstones, give room for three balloons.

Minor: up close there is faint mottled shading on the jaw, but it reads as clean-shaven at panel size. The banner hangs straight down from a crossbar instead of flying as in the other panels. Otherwise good: set jaw, diagonal shadow across the coat, grey topknot, tiny flush gold stud, uniform and chain. Sky between his head and the banner leaves room for the two off-panel balloons; tails point to the right edge, where he is looking.

Minor: the tali hangs on a thin gold cord instead of a clearly yellow thread. Her expression reads a little troubled more than purely weary. The head turn is a sideways glance rather than a full turn, but the beat still reads. Otherwise clean: she matches her sheet (indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, grey threading, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line). The courtyard, gatehouse and conch banner match the page, with no text on the banner, and the brass lamps have open wicks. Nagoji is correctly off-panel; he is placed off the left edge, toward the doorway and her gaze. The sky band across the top centre and right has room for all three short balloons.

Clean. Close on Revathi with a startled, newly seeing look toward Nagoji at frame right. All her bible details are present, including visible grey threading. Nagoji in the background matches (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, grey topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). He is drawn sharp, not soft, which is acceptable. Nagoji is visible, so the tail for his 'off' line goes to his mouth. Sky across the top leaves room for three balloons.

Clean. Wide two-shot across a long stretch of flagstone in the fort courtyard. The tiled gatehouse and the red conch banner are in place, in low gold evening light. Nagoji is in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain and boots, with a grey-streaked topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. Revathi is in the indigo-and-gold sari with the jasmine braid, grey threading, tali pendant, gold armlets and sandalwood line. Brass oil lamps have open flames. There is open sky in the upper centre for both balloons.

Acceptable. Revathi turns a step toward the open gate with her face in profile against the sunset. The courtyard, gatehouse, conch banner and lighting match panel 1. One small oddity: her tali-style pendant hangs down her back, not her front. It does not read as an error at panel size. The sky upper right, between her head and the flag, holds both balloons.

Acceptable. Revathi turns back over her shoulder toward the viewer and Nagoji, who is off-panel. The courtyard and gatehouse match the page. Her grey threading, jasmine braid, armlets, bangles and sandalwood line are correct, and her hand is sound. Again the pendant thread falls at her back (minor). There is sky upper right for her two balloons. Nagoji's balloon tails off the right edge, where he stood in panel 1.

Clean. Tight on Revathi with the flat-coin necklace, tali on its yellow thread, jhumkas, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line and gold armlets. The same gatehouse and banner sit at sunset behind her. The panel on the gatepost is a blank carved relief, not text. There is sky in the upper centre and upper right for both balloons.

Clean. Full-width final beat: Revathi walks out through the open gate into the low gold evening, small, with her back turned. Nagoji stands still in the near foreground, in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain and sword, with a grey-streaked topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. The conch banner flies above the gate. Upper-centre sky takes her two balloons trailing back toward him, and the open flagstones low in the centre take his caption.

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding curly hair, thin features, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus at his elbow. The commissioner wears a bag-wig, lace stock and dark cuffed coat, signs with a quill, and his tricorn is on the table. The soldiers wear blue coats, the treaty sheet is blank and there is no lettering. Caption space is fairly tight: use the roof and sky band along the top, between the soldiers' heads, plus the plain tablecloth at the front if needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji: white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, topknot with grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin and a small gold bead stud. Varma: aged face, grey low knot, shoulder cloth and sacred thread. Minor: Varma's mundu has a thin gold border instead of plain white, which is consistent with 8.3 and 8.4. There is a large clear night sky for the caption.

Acceptable. Varma is seen from behind at the wet parapet, looking out at the dark. He has a grey low knot and moustache, and the sacred thread shows across his back. The setting matches 8.2. Minor continuity point: the shoulder cloth from 8.2 is gone and he is bare-torsoed here, which fits the bible row and 8.4 and 8.5. There is wide sky above for both balloons.

Acceptable. Varma has turned from the parapet, his head turned toward the off-panel Nagoji. He has the aged face, grey low knot, sacred thread, no jewels and the same mundu as 8.2 and 8.3. Minor: the script's plain shoulder cloth is absent, consistent with 8.3 and 8.5. He has a white and red namam on his forehead, which matches his face-study sheet and is not banned for Varma. His hands are behind his back. The upper-right sky is clear for the balloon.

v02 is the only listed candidate, and it is clean. The shot is over Varma's shoulder onto Nagoji, framed close, and his expression gives nothing away. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch28 uniform row: Kerala topknot with no turban, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, a tiny flush gold stud, and the white coat with red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Varma matches the dedication look: grey hair in a low knot at the back, plain shoulder cloth, sacred thread, no jewels and no headwear. The setting fits the wet night rampart, with a brass oil lamp, distant hill forts and the camp's cookfires. There is no painted text, gore or anachronism, and both of Nagoji's hands are out of frame. The upper band of night sky is open from the top-left across to the centre, with room for all three balloons. Varma takes up more of the frame than the script's 'soft at the near edge' suggests, but the beat still reads clearly.

Minor only: Varma has a small Vaishnavite forehead mark and a pin-point ear stud (the dedication look says no jewels), and his shoulder cloth has a gold border rather than plain. Otherwise on beat: over-the-shoulder back view, grey low knot, sacred thread, wet parapet at night, distant fort lamps, road and camp cookfires, open-wick brass lamp. No painted text. Large clear dark sky upper right and centre for the three balloons.

Clean. Tight point-of-view shot of two aged, veined hands gripping the wet parapet. Hand anatomy is sound and the thumbs are on the correct sides. There are no rings or jewels, and the brass oil lamp has an open wick. The fort lamps, the road and the camp cookfires all match the setting. There is no text. Varma's head is off-panel behind the camera, so the tails point to the bottom edge between the two arms. Both medium balloons fit in the dark sky and the distant hill band across the top. Rendering is on the painterly-realistic side, but in line with the other candidates.

Minor: Varma's low knot is dark with grey streaks rather than fully grey as in 9.1 and 9.4. Otherwise on beat: close night face with a tear, sacred thread, plain shoulder cloth, wet parapet and camp lights. The memory bleeds in at the upper left as a ragged warm stain, not a framed flashback: young laughing Savitri, head thrown back, in a cream cloth with a red-and-gold border, gold earrings and necklace, no indigo, jasmine, tali or coin necklace. No painted text. Clear night sky upper right for the balloon.

Minor only. Varma matches the varma-v1 dedication face: grey low knot at the back, sacred thread, bare torso, no jewels or headwear. His head is in profile against the sky. One fist stays on the parapet while the other hand lies open, palm up, on the wet stone. Nagoji is small behind him and matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, topknot with grey at the temple, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. However, he is drawn sharp rather than out of focus. Varma's mundu has gold border stripes where the bible says plain. Both are small deviations. The upper sky above and right of Varma's head is wide, open space for the long and short balloons.

Minor: at this small scale Nagoji's ear ornament reads as a tiny pale bead just under the lobe, not a flush gold stud. It is a few pixels wide, so retouch it to a flush gold stud if possible. Nagoji has no grey at the temples. Varma's mundu has a gold border rather than plain, which matches the rest of the page. Otherwise on beat: wide 3:1 strip, Varma's arm opening toward the dark kingdom, fort lamps on far hills, the pale road, the camp cookfires, two small figures on the wet wall walk, Nagoji with a clean-shaven chin and thick moustache in the white coat and red waistcoat. No painted text. Wide clear sky band across the top for the balloon and two captions.

Minor: the camera is inside the chapel looking out at Nagoji in the doorway, not outside looking in, so the cross hangs on the inside wall rather than above the outer door. The beat still reads: De Lannoy kneels at the front pew, Duarte stands at the altar with hands raised (no Roman collar tab, ink-stained fingers) and Nagoji waits outside by the doorpost. Nagoji is on model, with a curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temples, topknot, red waistcoat and chain of office. The small brass altar crucifix and chalice are acceptable. The granite wall in the upper middle, between the door and Duarte, gives clear space for both captions.
